The Broken State of Freelance Payments

The $1.5T global freelance economy is held hostage by extractive Web2 middlemen, chargeback fraud, and opaque dispute arbitration.

💸

Extractive 10%–20% Platform Taxes

Legacy portals (Upwork, Fiverr) siphon up to 20% from service providers. Freelancers lose billions annually simply to secure basic payment guarantees.

⚠️

Chargeback Fraud & Payment Freezes

Traditional payment processors (PayPal, Stripe) allow unilateral 180-day clawbacks and arbitrary account freezes, leaving contractors unpaid after work delivery.

🏛️

Centralized Dispute Black-Boxes

When disagreements arise, anonymous customer support reps make arbitrary, unappealable rulings with zero cryptographic auditability, routinely siding with high-volume buyers.

⛓️

Fragile Web3 Escrow Alternatives

Existing Web3 escrows rely on complex token staking, external IPFS pinning gateways that suffer broken links, or multi-week DAO voting procedures that stall payouts.

Core Value Proposition
03 / 10

The Holdr Solution: Zero-Rent Escrow

A lightweight, trust-minimized escrow primitive engineered directly into Solidity with guaranteed dual timeouts and pull-based settlements.

🛡️

0% Protocol Fees

No platform tax, no cut, and no admin rent extraction. 100% of escrowed BOT transfers directly from buyer to seller.

📜

100% Onchain Strings

Titles, deliverables, delivery notes, and dispute reasons are stored directly in Solidity state as plain UTF-8. No IPFS or servers.

💰

Pull-Based Payouts

Reentrancy-hardened vault using pendingBalance and withdraw(). Reverting recipients cannot grief other parties.

⏱️

Guaranteed Timeouts

Overdue refunds, silent-buyer claims, and a 14-day arbiter 50/50 fallback split ensure nobody can be trapped forever.

Game Theory
07 / 10

Equilibrium & Anti-Griefing Safeguards

Engineered so no party—buyer, seller, or arbiter—can stall funds or maliciously freeze an escrow deal.

1. Mutual Arbiter Selection

The buyer names the arbiter during creation; the seller reviews the arbiter before initiating work. Arbiters possess fine-grained allocation control (0% to 100% to seller, remaining to buyer).

2. 14-Day Inactive Arbiter Defense

If an arbiter goes missing or refuses to rule, either the buyer or seller can invoke splitAfterArbiterTimeout() after 14 days, settling 50/50 with odd wei to buyer.

3. Silent Buyer Protection

If a buyer fails to review work within the review window (1–14 days), the seller can unilaterally claim the entire locked amount via claimAfterReview().

4. Malicious Recipient Isolation

Since all funds are credited to pendingBalance, an uncooperative contract that reverts upon receiving BOT cannot revert other users' deals or transactions.
